messages:
PagerDuty Bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT — inference-serving-prod (us-east-1) | error-rate 85% | 503s & CrashLoopBackOff on model-server pods. Oncall: Emma.
Emma: picking this up. seeing immediate 503 reports from the health endpoint. tagging @Maya @Josh. any quick wins? :eyes:
Maya: looking at pod list — lots of model-server pods in CrashLoopBackOff. kubectl logs show repeated CUDA OOM on init and then container restart.
Devin: confirmed. raw snippet from pod logs:
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:XXXX] failed to allocate 3.2GB (out of 8GB) -- CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Container crashed with signal 6
```
Maya: also seeing node pressure + recent scale events. autoscaler bumped node count from ~48 to 170 in ~4m (metrics look spiky) and then some nodes got evicted -> lots of pod restarts.
Josh: so this is thrash: rapid scale up -> noisy node provisioning -> pods scheduled to hosts with fragmented GPU memory -> OOMs -> crashloops -> autoscaler interprets as insufficient capacity -> scales further. vicious.
Emma: customer impact? Support Lead: multiple customers reporting timeouts on large generation requests, 15% of API calls returning 503 during the spike, latency tail >5s for gen requests. We have an active SLO impact.
Devin: immediate mitigations I'm trying: 1) pause cluster-autoscaler (prevent further noisy scale decisions), 2) set HPA maxReplicas lower for model-server to avoid simultaneous pod churn, 3) cordon the most recently provisioned nodes with kernel messages about nvlink errors.
Emma: do those now. exact cmds?
Devin: running:
```
kubectl annotate --overwrite deployment/model-server kubernetes.io/autoscaler-paused=true
kubectl patch hpa model-server -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":40}}'
kubectl cordon ip-10-1-78-225
```
Maya: also pushing out a conservative starter image for model-server that sets --max-batch-size=8 and disables speculative prefetch. less memory per process. preparing rollout.
Josh: agree. also recommending a short-term ASG cap at the cloud level to prevent explosive node adds. raising cloud cap to reduce churn is counterintuitive but we need to limit aggressive provisioning.
Emma: doing customer comms. Support Lead drafting status: "We are investigating GPU OOM crashes causing service instability; mitigations active; next update in 30m."
PagerDuty Bot: EMERGENCY CHANNEL OPEN — incident created: INC-20290315-047. Severity P1.
Devin: after pausing autoscaler and reducing HPA max, crashloop rate dropped ~60% within 2 minutes. pods that landed on cordoned nodes still restarting — evicting them for reschedule.
Maya: eviction command run for bad nodes, rescheduled pods landed on older stable nodes with bigger contiguous GPU memory — those pods came up healthy.
Emma: rolling the conservative image to 30% of model-server replicas as a canary. runbook link: <https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/serving/gpu-oom-thrash>.
Josh: action: add a temporary placement policy to prefer nodes with >12GB contiguous free GPU memory, and flag scheduling priorities so large-gen workloads go to dedicated pool. I'll open a ticket to formalize.
Devin: also enabling KV-prefix caching for chat workloads to reduce repeated token decode work — should shave peak GPU mem per request.
Support Lead: collecting list of impacted customers to notify (accounts flagged: acme-inc, atlasai, merchant-x). preparing targeted messages.
Emma: handoff — I'm on for next 30m to stabilize, then Josh takes over for mitigation and postmortem ownership. Maya will own runtime changes and patch rollout. Devin to follow up on autoscaler tuning. Support Lead to coordinate customer comms and status page.
Josh: noted. I'll keep the autoscaler paused and monitor node provisioning logs. if we see repeated CUDA driver errors on new nodes, we'll fallback to rolling out a lower-req instance type for the dedicated pool.
Maya: collecting logs and kernel traces for forensics; snapshotting affected nodes.
Devin: left a quick snippet added to incident channel for quick revert:
```
# rollback conservative image
kubectl set image deployment/model-server model-server=registry.redwood/model-server:stable
# unpause autoscaler once stable
kubectl annotate --overwrite deployment/model-server kubernetes.io/autoscaler-paused=false
```
Emma: next update in 20m unless major regressions. nice quick triage everyone. :thumbsup:
Ops Bot: incident timeline note saved (INC-20290315-047) — paused autoscaler at 2029-03-15T04:07:12Z, HPA max set 40, 7 nodes cordoned, 12 pods evicted.
Support Lead: created customer notification and posted to status page.
Emma: handing to Josh now — leaving the channel, logging handoff in post-incident doc.
Josh: taking over. will keep monitoring for 2h and start RCA draft when stable.
Maya: continuing log collection and kernel dumps. will ping if we need a driver rollback or node image rollback.
PagerDuty Bot: incident acknowledged by Emma; reassigned to Josh.
summary: GPU OOM + autoscaler thrash led to CrashLoopBackOffs and customer-facing 503s. Immediate mitigations: paused autoscaler, lowered HPA max, cordoned/evicted unstable nodes, rolled conservative image canary, customer notifications and handoff to infra owner for RCA.
